vectors.name: least_squares_single_fit_asymmetric_alphas
vectors._comment: 15 uniform-t samples of the cubic (0,0) (5,5) (20,100) (100,100). The first fit is accepted (max squared error 17.069473 < error 20), so this vector gates generate_bezier's least-squares solve on a genuinely non-collinear input: alpha_l = 55.33, alpha_r = 65.76. The alpha < epsilon fallback would put both controls at chord/3 = 47.14 along the tangents, and swapping alpha_l with alpha_r moves each control by 10.4 - both far outside the 0.5 gate tolerance.

vectors.name: reparameterized_single_fit
vectors._comment: error 4.0 puts the initial max squared error (9.50) at/above error and below error*error = 16, which is the only window in which the reparameterize loop runs at all - with error <= 1 that window is empty, which is why every earlier vector in this file skipped it. One Newton-Raphson pass moves the parameters by up to 0.0159 and drops the error to 2.53 < 4, giving ONE segment. A reparameterize (or newton_raphson) that returned u unchanged leaves the error at 9.50, exhausts the 4 iterations and splits into 2 segments.

vectors.name: split_at_max_error_index_not_midpoint
vectors._comment: the same 13 points at error 1.0: error*error == error, so the reparameterize window is empty and the fit goes straight to the recursive split. The split lands on index 2 - the max-error point - not on the midpoint index 6, so the junction is (4.62963, 35.185185). Splitting at the midpoint instead, or failing to negate the centre tangent for the right-hand sub-fit, changes the segments well beyond tolerance.

vectors.name: asymmetric_s_curve_recursive_splits
vectors._comment: an S-curve that recurses to 4 segments. Deliberately ASYMMETRIC: a mirror-symmetric S-curve produces max-error ties whose runner-up gap is about 1e-13, i.e. a few ULP, which Rust's sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) and Swift's hypot could resolve differently; here the worst runner-up gap is 13% of the winning distance.

vectors.name: right_angle_corner_collinear_fallback
vectors._comment: five collinear points, a right-angle corner, then three collinear. The only vector in this file that reaches generate_bezier's alpha < epsilon fallback: on the [5..7] sub-fit the chord parameters are exactly 0, 0.5, 1, so b1 = b2 = 0.375 at the middle point, the C matrix rows are identical, det_C0_C1 is exactly 0 and both alphas are 0. The fallback then places the controls at chord/3 = 8 along the tangents: (40,20) and (40,28).

vectors.name: reparam_two_iterations_single_fit
vectors._comment: converges only on the SECOND Newton pass (max squared error 22.79 then 7.35, against error 15), so it pins a reparameterize loop of at least 2 iterations: a single-iteration loop splits instead of accepting one segment.

vectors.name: reparam_exhausts_iterations_then_splits
vectors._comment: the other side of that loop: all four iterations run (7.98, 6.58, 6.02, 5.73) and none reaches error 4.5, so the fit falls through to the recursive split. NOTE: u is NOT carried forward - after the loop only split_point is read, and each recursive child re-derives u from chord_length_parameterize, so the final `u = u_prime` is a dead store. 2 segments.
